product_desc: sliced napa cabbage kimchi in a shallow white bowl, leaves deep red with chilli paste and the white stems still crisp, red brine pooling at the base, no jar and no packaging anywhere in frame
cook: a young Korean cook in his twenties in a plain apron, quick and relaxed
kitchen: a small apartment kitchen with pale tiles and a gas hob, a wooden board on the counter, neutral daylight from a window on the left, warm only in the shadows
prep_subject: beef cut into small dice about one centimetre on a wooden board, and beside it a bowl of kimchi that has already been chopped down into small loose pieces the same size as the beef dice or smaller, a scattered heap of separate red-stained fragments with pale stem flecks through it. There are no whole leaves, no folded leaves and no long strips left: the leaf shape is gone entirely and what remains looks like a coarse red relish. Also on the counter a bowl of plain steamed white rice that is clearly the largest quantity, two whole eggs in their shells, chopped spring onion, and a small dish of gochujang with sesame oil
prep_defines: the one-centimetre beef dice, the finer half-centimetre kimchi chop, and the rice being the largest quantity
cook_vessel: a carbon steel wok over a gas flame
cook_subject: the wok partway through, holding exactly two ingredients and nothing else at all. On one side, small one-centimetre cubes of beef already browned on every face. On the other, kimchi that has already been chopped down into small loose pieces the same size as the beef dice or smaller, a scattered heap of separate red-stained fragments with pale stem flecks through it. There are no whole leaves, no folded leaves and no long strips left: the leaf shape is gone entirely and what remains looks like a coarse red relish, in a modest amount that covers less of the wok than the beef does. Those two things are the entire contents of the wok. No rice, no egg and no other ingredient is in the wok
cook_negatives: whole kimchi leaves, folded leaves, long kimchi strips, kimchi pieces larger than the beef dice, beef in thin slices, more kimchi than rice, egg in the wok with the rice, scrambled egg, rice cakes, tteokbokki, rice added before the kimchi is fried, wet clumped rice
vessel_start: empty except for a film of oil just beginning to shimmer, no food in it yet
hero_subject: the finished fried rice, everything tossed together and completely mixed so it is one uniform orange-red mass with no separate sections and no ingredients arranged in piles. Rice is clearly the bulk; small cubes of browned beef and fine pieces of kimchi are distributed evenly through it as flecks. Every grain is separate and stained orange-red. It is mounded in a shallow bowl with a single fried egg laid on the centre, its white set and lacy at the edges and its yolk whole and unbroken, chopped spring onion and toasted sesame scattered over
hero_setting: a wooden dining table away from the cooking area, laid for eating: the bowl sits on the table top with a spoon and chopsticks beside it and a glass of water behind. There is no stove, no hob, no gas burner, no wok and no cooking equipment anywhere in frame, and the table is clearly a place to eat rather than a place to cook. Neutral daylight from a window
story: diced beef into an empty hot wok and browned on every face
fine chopped kimchi in beside it, then the rice, tossed until red
bowled, an egg fried and slid on top, yolk whole
first_heat: The small beef cubes hit the bare hot steel and sear at once, browning at their corners with a hard fast sizzle.
transform: the beef finishes browning on every face and is pushed aside, the finely chopped kimchi goes in beside it and fries from bright red to a darker glossy red as its brine cooks off, and then the steamed rice goes in, far more of it than either, and is tossed until every grain takes the colour and turns orange-red.
lift: A wok spatula enters from the left, lifts a portion of fried rice clear of the wok and holds it at the centre of frame. The grains fall loose and separate off the edge of the spatula, small beef cubes and fine kimchi visible through them.
plate: The hands of <Subject 1> enter from the top of frame holding the wok by its handle, tip it once over the shallow bowl, and the fried rice slides out in one mound. The hands withdraw out of frame.
final_lift: A hand enters from the right holding a spoon, breaks the whole yolk over the rice and lifts one spoonful clear of the bowl, holding it steady at the centre of frame with the yolk running down through the orange-red grains.

beats.c1s1: <Subject 1> draws the board of diced beef and the bowl of chopped kimchi toward them in one movement.
beats.c1s2: Both hands of <Subject 1> loosen the steamed rice with a spoon until the grains fall apart rather than holding together, then slide the bowl to the near edge beside the kimchi and the beef.
beats.c1s3: The hands of <Subject 1> enter from the top of frame carrying the diced beef alone, tip it into the empty hot wok in one movement, and withdraw straight up out of frame empty. No kimchi, no rice and no egg go in during this shot.
beats.c3s2: The hand of <Subject 1> enters from the top of frame holding the pan, tips it once over the mounded rice, and a whole fried egg slides off it onto the centre of the bowl, its white set and lacy at the edges and its yolk unbroken. The hand withdraws straight up out of frame with the empty pan.

clip02_shot1: [Shot 1] Locked-off close-up at wok height, 50mm feel, continuing directly from <Picture 1>. The wok of <Picture 4> fills the lower two thirds of frame over its burner, which stays visible at the bottom of frame throughout. The beef from clip 01 is browned and pushed to one side of the wok. The hands of <Subject 1> enter from the top of frame carrying the bowl of chopped kimchi from <Picture 3>, tip it into the clear side of the wok in one movement, and withdraw straight up out of frame empty. The kimchi hits the hot steel and its brine begins to cook off at once. No rice is in this shot. The camera does not move at any point in this shot, and the framing does not drift.
negatives_global: bibimbap, ingredients arranged in separate sections or piles, rice cakes, tteokbokki, a stew or hot pot, a deep pot, soup or broth, wet clumped rice, instant noodles, processed cheese
sound_01: A small apartment kitchen with a low room tone. In the first shot, a bowl set down on a wooden board. In the second shot, a spoon loosening steamed rice in a bowl. In the third shot, a gas burner rising, then a hard fast sizzle as thin beef meets bare hot steel. No speech.
sound_02: A hard continuous stir fry throughout, the scrape of a spatula against carbon steel. In the first shot, wet kimchi hitting hot metal with a sharp burst of steam. In the second shot the sound dries out as the brine cooks off and the rice goes in. No speech.
sound_03: An apartment kitchen. In the first shot, fried rice sliding from a wok into a ceramic bowl in one mass. In the second shot, an egg crackling in a hot pan and then sliding off it onto the rice. In the third shot, a spoon breaking a yolk, and the bowl settling on wood. No speech.
music: A bright young bed: a clipped drum groove under a warm bass line, quick and easy, the feeling of a fast weeknight meal.
